title: Robert Griffin III set to interview for head coaching job at Baylor
content:
Former Baylor quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner Robert Griffin III is expected to interview for the head coaching job at his alma mater, sources familiar with the hiring process confirmed to The Athletic. On3 was the first to report the news.

Griffin, who starred at Baylor from 2008-11 and won the school’s first and only Heisman, works as a television analyst for Fox Sports. He has no collegiate coaching experience but said last month that he is “100 percent” interested in the job.

“If Baylor wants to get back to winning and have a university that isn’t just respectable on the football field but that fans can be proud of, they need people who know what it looks like to win at Baylor,” Griffin said in an interview on “The Dan Patrick Show.”

“So yeah, I would 100 percent be interested.”

Griffin said last month that he had already spoken with athletic director Doug McNamee, who announced on Oct. 25 that Baylor was moving on from head coach Dave Aranda. Aranda went 40-40 in six-plus seasons with the Bears and could never keep things rolling after a breakout 12-2 season in 2021.

Baylor interviewing Griffin comes on the heels of former NC State star quarterback Philip Rivers formally accepting the head football coaching job at his alma mater. Hiring coaches with NFL ties but no college coaching experience has become a recent trend, with Bill Belichick (North Carolina), Michael Vick (Norfolk State), DeSean Jackson (Delaware State) and Deion Sanders (Jackson State) all taking over programs since 2020.

Rivers also has no college coaching experience but has coached high school football in Alabama since 2021.

“The way that coaching happens, being a CEO type of coach in college football is completely different,” Griffin said about the sport’s current landscape. “You don’t have to have experience coaching at the highest level to be successful, and I’m just tired of seeing Baylor be the stepstone or the stepchild to all these other teams. We should be back on top.”

Griffin, a Texas native, led Baylor to 10 wins in 2011 and finished that season with 4,293 passing yards, a 72.4 percent completion rate and 37 touchdowns against six interceptions. He finished his Baylor career with 10,366 yards passing and 2,254 yards rushing. He went No. 2 to Washington in the 2012 NFL Draft and played 56 games over seven NFL seasons, ending in 2020.

Griffin also endorsed a few sitting college coaches for the Bears job.

“I would also advocate for Spencer Danielson, the head coach at Boise State,” Griffin said. “I think he is a top-notch guy, a top-notch coach who knows how to win. I also think Jeff Traylor at UTSA is a great option. A dark horse would be Lincoln Riley from USC.

“I think Baylor is a great job. It’s a university that obviously I hold very near and dear to my heart.”

— Bruce Feldman contributed to this story.
